entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Epictetus was a Greek Stoic philosopher who spent most of his life in Nicopolis in northwestern Greece after being banished from Rome.

Born into slavery at Hierapolis, Phrygia around 55 CE, Epictetus rose to prominence as a teacher and became one of the most influential Stoics of all time.

He was a key figure in the development of Stoic philosophy, which emphasized reason, self-control, and indifference to external events.

Epictetus' teachings were highly influential in the Roman Empire and beyond, shaping the thoughts and actions of numerous prominent figures, including Emperor Marcus Aurelius.

Epictetus' legacy extends far beyond his own time, with his ideas continuing to inspire philosophers, politicians, and ordinary people to this day.

Despite the passage of centuries, Epictetus' message of inner strength, resilience, and personal responsibility remains as relevant and powerful as ever.
